mainTopic: יהושע בן גמלא's school system, why neighbors cannot block teaching children Torah, and רבא's rules for running children's schools
overview: The גמרא explains the end of the משנה, which says neighbors cannot object to the noise of schoolchildren. That rule comes from the תקנה of יהושע בן גמלא. רב tells the history of Jewish education in stages: first only fathers taught, then teachers were set up in ירושלים, then in every region for teens, and finally יהושע בן גמלא set up teachers in every town for children of six or seven. רב also gives a teacher practical advice about starting age, gentle discipline and keeping weaker students in class. The גמרא then answers three ברייתות that seem to let neighbors block a children's teacher. It explains that they are talking about teachers of non-Jewish children or the town scribe. Next, רבא gives practical rules about where children may be sent to learn, class size, and replacing teachers. רב דימי מנהרדעא disagrees with him twice about how to choose a teacher. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a proof for רב דימי from יואב's war against אדום, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the משנה is about schoolchildren after יהושע בן גמלא's enactment
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the משנה, where neighbors cannot object to noise, is about תינוקות של בית רבן, and it applies from the time of יהושע בן גמלא's תקנה onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part of the משנה is talking about schoolchildren, and it applies from the time of יהושע בן גמלא's enactment onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the end of the משנה lets someone teach children even though the neighbors are bothered by the noise. It is answering an earlier question about why the start and end of the משנה seem to rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The start of the משנה lets neighbors object to noise, but the end does not. The answer is that the end is about teaching Torah to children. Ever since יהושע בן גמלא's enactment required teachers in every town, neighbors cannot block this kind of teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause, the end part of a משנה or ברייתא
We have come to, meaning this part is talking about a specific case
Schoolchildren, young children learning Torah with a teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reason a Torah teacher of children may teach in a shared space even when the neighbors complain.

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
phrases.english: The latter clause: we have arrived at schoolchildren,
phrases.notes: The סיפא is the end of our משנה, which says neighbors can't object to the noise of children learning.

phrases.english: and from the enactment of Yehoshua ben Gamla onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about the difference between the start and the end of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the סיפא is about schoolchildren under a later enactment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The start and end of the משנה seem to contradict each other about noise.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end is about teaching children Torah, which יהושע בן גמלא's תקנה protects, so neighbors cannot object.

steps.title: רב praises יהושע בן גמלא for saving the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: יהושע בן גמלא should be remembered for good, because without him Torah would have been forgotten from ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: That man should truly be remembered for good, and his name is יהושע בן גמלא. If not for him, the Torah would have been forgotten from the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing what יהושע בן גמלא's enactment was and how important it was. This opens a history lesson that continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the 'enactment' mentioned in step 1. רב opens with high praise, which tells us the enactment was not a small detail. It was what kept Torah alive among the Jewish people.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Truly, that man is remembered for good,
and Yehoshua ben Gamla is his name,
for were it not for him,
Torah would have been forgotten from Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the enactment of יהושע בן גמלא that step 1 mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע בן גמלא's enactment saved Torah from being forgotten in ישראל.

steps.title: First stage: only fathers taught their own sons
steps.stepSummary: At first, a father taught his son Torah, so orphans did not learn at all. This was based on reading ולמדתם אתם, 'you yourselves shall teach'.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, whoever had a father was taught Torah by him, and whoever had no father did not learn Torah. What did they expound? 'And you shall teach them', read as 'you yourselves shall teach'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב describes the first stage of Jewish education, where teaching was only the father's job. The גמרא also gives the פסוק they used to explain why they did it that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read the פסוק as putting the מצוה on the fathers themselves. That left a big gap: a boy without a father had nobody to teach him. This problem drives each of the later changes.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they expound? Which פסוק did they learn this from?

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says אֹתָם ('them', the children), but the דרשה reads it as אַתֶּם ('you', the fathers). This is a play on the similar spelling, not what the word plainly means.

phrases.english: For at first, whoever had a father —
he would teach him Torah;
whoever did not have a father —
would not learn Torah.
What did they expound?
"And you shall teach them" — and you yourselves shall teach.
phrases.notes: דברים 11:19. They read אֹתָם, 'them', as if it said אַתֶּם, 'you'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the history that explains why יהושע בן גמלא was needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally only fathers taught Torah, based on ולמדתם אתם, so orphans were left out.

steps.title: Second stage: teachers set up in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: They enacted that teachers of children be set up in ירושלים, based on the פסוק כי מציון תצא תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They enacted that teachers of children should be set up in ירושלים. What did they expound? 'For from ציון the Torah will go out'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב describes the first fix: a central place in ירושלים where children could be taught. The גמרא again gives the פסוק behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now a child no longer needed a father who could teach him himself. A teacher was available in ירושלים. The choice of ירושלים comes from the פסוק saying Torah goes out from ציון.

phrases.english: They enacted that they should set up
teachers of children in Jerusalem.
What did they expound?
"For from Zion shall go forth Torah."

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מוֹשִׁיבִין מְלַמְּדֵי תִינוֹקוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first fix for the problem of children without fathers described in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teachers of children were set up in ירושלים, based on כי מציון תצא תורה.

steps.title: Third stage: a school in every region for teenagers
steps.stepSummary: Orphans still could not get to ירושלים, so teachers were set up in every פלך, and students began at about sixteen or seventeen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, whoever had a father would bring him up to ירושלים and have him taught, while whoever had no father would not go up and learn. So they enacted that teachers be set up in every region, and they brought the students in at about sixteen or seventeen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב shows that the ירושלים fix did not fully work, and describes the next fix: local schools in each region.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having teachers only in ירושלים still left orphans out, because someone had to bring the child up there. Putting schools in every region brought learning closer. But students started very late, at sixteen or seventeen, and that sets up the next problem.

phrases.english: But still, whoever had a father —
he would bring him up and have him taught;
whoever did not have a father —
would not go up and learn.

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מוֹשִׁיבִין בְּכׇל פֶּלֶךְ וּפֶלֶךְ.
phrases.english: They enacted that they should set up teachers in each and every region.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַכְנִיסִין אוֹתָן כְּבֶן שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה כְּבֶן שְׁבַע עֶשְׂרֵה,
phrases.english: And they would bring them in at about age sixteen or seventeen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the weakness of the ירושלים system and describes the next fix.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teachers were set up in every region, but students only started at sixteen or seventeen.

steps.title: יהושע בן גמלא sets up teachers in every town for young children
steps.stepSummary: Teenage students rebelled and left when the teacher got angry, until יהושע בן גמלא set up teachers in every province and town, starting children at six or seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a student whose teacher got angry at him would kick back at him and leave. This went on until יהושע בן גמלא came and enacted that teachers of children be set up in every province and every town, and they would bring the children in at about six or seven.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes the history with the last problem and יהושע בן גמלא's final enactment. This is the enactment step 1 was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Older teens who had never been in school would rebel against a strict teacher and walk out. יהושע בן גמלא fixed both problems at once: teachers in every town, so everyone could reach one, and a starting age of six or seven, when children still accept discipline. Because this system is for everyone, neighbors cannot stop it.
steps.whatToRemember: Education went through four stages: fathers only, then ירושלים, then each region for teens, then every town for six- and seven-year-olds. The last stage came from יהושע בן גמלא, and because of it a teacher of children may teach even when the neighbors complain about the noise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for setting up teachers of children in every town, and it explains the rule in the סיפא of the משנה.

phrases.english: And one whose teacher would get angry at him —
would kick at him and leave.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן גַּמְלָא וְתִיקֵּן,
phrases.english: Until Yehoshua ben Gamla came and enacted
that they should set up teachers of children

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה וּבְכׇל עִיר וָעִיר,
phrases.english: in each and every province and in each and every town,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַכְנִיסִין אוֹתָן כְּבֶן שֵׁשׁ כְּבֶן שֶׁבַע.
phrases.english: and they would bring them in at about age six or seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁבָּא יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן גַּמְלָא וְתִיקֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the problem with the regional system and gives the final enactment of יהושע בן גמלא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יהושע בן גמלא established teachers of children in every province and town, starting at age six or seven. That is the enactment behind the סיפא of the משנה.

steps.title: Start children at six, then teach them a lot
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רב שמואל בר שילת not to accept students under six. From six on, he should accept them and fill them with Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רב שמואל בר שילת: Don't take a child before age six. From then on, take him and stuff him with learning like you'd feed an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a children's teacher practical advice about when to start a child in school.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits with יהושע בן גמלא's rule from Step 6 that children start at six or seven. רב adds two sides: don't start too early, but once the child is ready, teach him as much as he can take in.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of young children who gets advice from רב
Stuff him like an ox, meaning feed him a lot of Torah

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת:
phrases.english: Rav said to Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat:
Until six, do not accept [a student];
from here on, accept [him],
and stuff him like an ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds practical guidance about the starting age set by יהושע בן גמלא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not accept a student under six. From six on, accept him and teach him intensively.

steps.title: Discipline gently and keep weaker students in class
steps.stepSummary: רב tells the teacher to hit a child only with a sandal strap. A student who can't learn yet should still stay with his classmates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב also told him: When you hit a child, only use a sandal strap. Whoever can read will read. Whoever can't read should stay as a companion to his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives two more teaching tips: be gentle when you discipline, and don't throw out a weak student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the problem in Step 6, where students ran away when the teacher got angry. Here, discipline is kept light, with just a sandal strap. The student who isn't reading yet stays in class, because being around the others helps him.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's teaching advice: start at six, teach a lot, discipline only lightly, and keep weaker students in the group.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת:
phrases.english: And Rav said to Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat:
When you strike a child,
strike only with the strap of a sandal.
One who reads, let him read;
one who does not read, let him be a companion to his friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: More advice from רב to the same teacher
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hit a child only with a sandal strap. A student who isn't reading yet should still stay in the class.

steps.title: A ברייתא says neighbors can stop a children's teacher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if someone in a shared courtyard wants to become a doctor, bloodletter, weaver, or children's teacher, the neighbors can stop him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If one of the people in a courtyard wants to become a doctor, a bloodletter, a weaver, or a teacher of children, the other courtyard members can stop him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that nobody can block a teacher of children. This ברייתא lists a children's teacher among the jobs that neighbors are allowed to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These jobs bring in lots of people and noise, so neighbors can object. The problem is that the ברייתא includes a children's teacher in the list. That seems to say Torah classes can be blocked too, which goes against the importance of children's Torah learning in this סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
The people who share a courtyard
They can stop him, they can prevent it

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One of the members of a courtyard
who wished to become a doctor,
a bloodletter, a weaver, or a teacher of children –
the members of the courtyard can prevent him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea that a children's Torah teacher can't be blocked
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 1 that the סיפא of the משנה, where neighbors cannot object, is about teaching schoolchildren under יהושע בן גמלא's תקנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts a children's teacher on the list of jobs that neighbors can block.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about teaching non-Jewish children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a teacher of non-Jewish children.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A teacher of non-Jewish children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neighbors can stop a teacher of non-Jewish children, because that class isn't the Torah teaching that יהושע בן גמלא set up. Teaching Jewish children Torah still can't be blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
With non-Jewish children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a narrow case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא meant any teacher of children, including Torah teachers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means a teacher of non-Jewish children. A Jewish children's Torah teacher can't be blocked.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: one neighbor can stop the other
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that when two people share a courtyard, one can stop the other from becoming a children's teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Two people live in a courtyard, and one of them wants to become a doctor, a bloodletter, a weaver, or a teacher of children. The other one can stop him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same problem. Here even one neighbor alone can block a children's teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a stronger case. Even a single neighbor can object, so the same question comes back: how can a children's Torah teacher be blocked?

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a new source is coming)

phrases.english: Come and hear: Two who live in a courtyard,
and one of them wished to become a doctor,
or a bloodletter, or a weaver, or a teacher of children –
his fellow can prevent him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge with the same point as Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a children's Torah teacher can't be blocked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even one neighbor can stop someone from teaching children.

steps.title: Same answer: non-Jewish children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer. This ברייתא is also about teaching non-Jewish children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about non-Jewish children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge exactly the way it answered the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added. The ברייתא is again limited to a teacher of non-Jewish children, so Torah teaching for Jewish children stays protected.

phrases.english: Here too, with non-Jewish children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from Step 10 again for the challenge in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a narrow case (same as before)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even one neighbor can block any children's teacher.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a teacher of non-Jewish children can be blocked.

steps.title: A third ברייתא names a Jewish teacher
steps.stepSummary: A third ברייתא says that someone with a house in a shared courtyard may not rent it to a doctor, bloodletter, weaver, Jewish סופר, or non-Jewish סופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone who has a house in a shared courtyard may not rent it to a doctor, a bloodletter, a weaver, a Jewish סופר, or a non-Jewish סופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a harder challenge. This ברייתא lists a Jewish סופר separately, so the answer 'non-Jewish children' no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סופר here means a children's teacher, then a Jewish teacher is clearly being blocked. The earlier answer can't explain this, because the ברייתא mentions the Jewish one and the non-Jewish one as two separate cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard owned together by partners

steps.confusionAlert: The word סופר can mean a children's teacher or a writer of documents. The whole question here depends on which meaning is right.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בַּיִת
phrases.english: Come and hear: One who has a house
in a jointly owned courtyard –

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יַשְׂכִּירֶנּוּ לֹא לְרוֹפֵא,
phrases.english: he may not rent it out, not to a doctor,
nor to a bloodletter, nor to a weaver,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לְסוֹפֵר יְהוּדִי, וְלֹא לְסוֹפֵר אַרְמַאי!
phrases.english: nor to a Jewish sofer, nor to a non-Jewish sofer!
phrases.notes: The challenge reads סופר as a children's teacher. Since a Jewish one is named, 'non-Jewish children' won't answer it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge that gets around the earlier answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a Jewish children's Torah teacher can't be blocked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא names a Jewish סופר separately from a non-Jewish one, so it can't be talking only about non-Jewish children.

steps.title: The סופר here is the town scribe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the town scribe, not a children's teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? The town scribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge by explaining that סופר here means the town's scribe, not a teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The town scribe isn't teaching Torah to children, and he brings in a lot of visitors, so neighbors can stop him. Teaching Jewish children Torah in a courtyard still can't be blocked.
steps.whatToRemember: All three challenges are answered. Neighbors can block a teacher of non-Jewish children or the town scribe, but not a teacher of Jewish children learning Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far יהושע בן גמלא's enactment reaches. Teaching Torah to children is so important that neighbors' normal right to object to noise doesn't apply to it.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
With the town scribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads a word differently (סופר means scribe, not teacher)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סופר יהודי means a Jewish children's teacher, so Torah teaching could be blocked.
steps.terutzMaskana: סופר means the town scribe. A Jewish children's Torah teacher still can't be blocked.

steps.title: Where a child may be sent to learn
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that after the תקנה of יהושע בן גמלא, a child is not sent from one town to another to learn. A child may be sent from one synagogue to another, but not across a river unless there is a solid bridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since the תקנה of יהושע בן גמלא, we do not send a child from his town to another town to learn. But we do send him from one synagogue to another. If a river separates them, we don't send him. If there is a proper bridge, we do. If there is only a narrow plank, we don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section of practical rules from רבא about children's schooling. This first rule is about how far a young child may be sent to study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once יהושע בן גמלא required teachers in every town, there is no need to send small children to another town, so each child learns where he lives. Within one town a child may go to a different synagogue school. Safety still matters, so a river blocks this unless there is a real bridge.

keyTerms.meaning: The enactment of יהושע בן גמלא requiring teachers of children in every town
A synagogue, which also served as the school

steps.confusionAlert: The word גַּמְלָא at the end is not the name גמלא from יהושע בן גמלא, and it is not a camel. Here it means a narrow, shaky bridge.

phrases.english: Rava said:
From the ordinance of Yehoshua ben Gamla onward,
phrases.notes: This is the rule that every town must appoint teachers for children, which the גמרא described earlier.

phrases.english: we do not bring a child from town to town;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִבֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא – מַמְטִינַן.
phrases.english: but from synagogue to synagogue, we do bring him.
phrases.notes: The children learned in the synagogue, so 'synagogue' here really means a school inside the same town.

phrases.english: And if a river separates them, we do not bring him.
And if there is a bridge, we do bring him.
And if there is only a narrow plank, we do not bring him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִתַּקָּנַת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן גַּמְלָא וְאֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the courtyard קשיות and answers to a new set of practical rules about children's education.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child is educated in his own town. He may move between synagogue schools in that town, but not across a river without a proper bridge.

steps.title: How many students one teacher may have
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one teacher handles up to twenty-five children. With fifty children, two teachers are hired. With forty, an assistant is added and the town helps pay for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: A children's teacher can take up to twenty-five students. If there are fifty, we appoint two teachers. If there are forty, we appoint an assistant, and the town helps pay for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second practical rule, this time about class size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty-five is the most one teacher can handle properly. Fifty is enough for two full classes, so two teachers are hired. Forty is too many for one teacher but not enough for two full classes, so the solution is an assistant, paid partly by the town.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The number for a teacher of children
is twenty-five children.
And if there are fifty, we appoint two teachers;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִיכָּא אַרְבְּעִין – מוֹקְמִינַן רֵישׁ דּוּכְנָא,
phrases.english: and if there are forty, we set up an assistant,
and the town helps him with the cost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical rule from רבא in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Up to 25 students per teacher. Fifty means two teachers. Forty means a teacher plus an assistant funded with the town's help.

steps.title: Don't replace a teacher with a better one
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a teacher is doing his job and a better teacher becomes available, the first teacher is not removed. Otherwise the new one may become lazy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: If there is a children's teacher who teaches, and another one comes along who teaches more than him, we do not remove the first one. Perhaps the new one will become lazy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third rule: a working teacher is not fired just because someone better shows up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the town should always grab the best teacher. רבא worries that a new teacher who knows he has no competition could slack off. So the first teacher keeps his job.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A teacher of children who teaches,
and there is another who teaches more than him,
we do not remove the first one,
since perhaps the other will come to be lazy.
phrases.notes: The worry is about the new teacher: with no one to compete with, he might stop trying hard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַקְרֵי יָנוֹקֵי דְּגָרֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third practical rule from רבא, now about replacing teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A working teacher is not replaced by a better one, because the replacement may become lax.

steps.title: רב דימי says rivalry makes teachers better
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא disagrees with רבא. The new teacher will teach even better, because competition among teachers increases wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: All the more so he will teach better, because jealousy among teachers increases wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי מנהרדעא argues on רבא's last rule about replacing a teacher with a better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא feared the new teacher would slack off. רב דימי says the opposite: the rivalry with the teacher who was let go keeps the new one sharp. So there is no reason not to hire the better teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: רב דימי from the city of נהרדעא

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a pattern: רבא and רב דימי disagree twice in a row about how to choose teachers.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a said:
All the more so he will teach more,
for jealousy among teachers increases wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּגָרֵיס טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's reasoning in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The better teacher may replace the first one. Competition will keep him working hard.

steps.title: Hire the teacher who covers more
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that when choosing between a teacher who covers a lot but is not precise and one who is precise but covers little, we hire the one who covers more. Mistakes will fix themselves over time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: There are two children's teachers. One covers a lot but is not exact. The other is exact but does not cover much. We hire the one who covers a lot but is not exact. Mistakes go away on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a rule for choosing between two teachers with different strengths: amount of learning or accuracy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא values how much the children learn. He holds that small errors will get corrected naturally later on, so covering more material is the bigger gain.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
These two teachers of children:
one covers a lot but is not precise,
and one is precise but does not cover a lot;
we appoint the one who covers a lot but is not precise;
an error goes away by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי תְּרֵי מַקְרֵי דַרְדְּקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבא's series of rules after רב דימי's disagreement, with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prefer the teacher who covers more material, because errors correct themselves.

steps.title: רב דימי says hire the precise teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא disagrees again. We hire the precise teacher, because once a mistake is learned, it stays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: We appoint the one who is exact even though he covers less. Once a mistake gets in, it stays in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי מנהרדעא argues on רבא's rule about which teacher to hire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said errors fix themselves. רב דימי says the opposite: a mistake a child learns gets stuck in his mind. So accuracy matters more than the amount of material.

keyTerms.meaning: Once it has entered, it has entered (it stays)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא and רב דימי disagree twice. On replacing a teacher, רבא worries the new one will slack off, while רב דימי trusts competition. On choosing a teacher, רבא prefers more material because errors fix themselves, while רב דימי prefers accuracy because errors stick.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a said:
We appoint the one who is precise but does not cover a lot;
an error, once it has entered, has entered.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר: מוֹתְבִינַן דְּדָיֵיק וְלָא גָּרֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's ruling in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prefer the precise teacher, because a learned error does not go away.

steps.title: A proof begins from יואב's war against אדום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב דימי מנהרדעא with a פסוק saying that יואב killed every male in אדום. It then begins telling what happened when יואב came back to דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'For יואב and all ישראל stayed there six months, until he had cut off every male in אדום.' When יואב came before דוד, דוד said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a proof for רב דימי מנהרדעא by quoting a פסוק about יואב killing every male in אדום. It then sets up a conversation between דוד and יואב, which continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי said a mistake learned from a teacher stays with the student, so precision matters most. This story will show a real case where a word learned the wrong way led to a big real-world result. Pay attention to the word זָכָר (male), because the proof will turn on it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
Male; the key word in this story
The nation יואב went to war against
Before him, in front of him

steps.confusionAlert: At this point it is not yet clear how this פסוק proves anything about teachers. Don't worry, the conversation between דוד and יואב in the next lines makes the connection.

phrases.english: As it is written: "For six months
Yoav and all Israel remained there,
until he had cut off every male in Edom."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 11:16. Keep an eye on the word "male"; it becomes important in a moment.

phrases.english: When he came before David,
phrases.notes: "He" means יואב, coming back from the war.

phrases.english: he said to him:
phrases.notes: דוד is the one speaking here, and his words continue in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a supporting source from a פסוק for רב דימי מנהרדעא's claim in Step 20 that a learned mistake stays.
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי מנהרדעא's position that we hire the precise teacher, because once a mistake is learned it stays.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in מלכים א 11:16 about יואב cutting off every male in אדום, followed by the story of his meeting with דוד.
